question: What does the intraarticular route of medication administration involve?

options.A: Delivering drugs through the skin using a patch
options.B: Swallowing pills for systemic joint relief
options.C: Administering medicine into a muscle belly
options.D: Injecting medication directly into a joint space

explanation: Intraarticular simply means putting the drug straight inside the joint cavity. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h1)

question: Why is the intraarticular route preferred for treating a single inflamed joint?

options.A: It prevents any risk of local infection at the injection site
options.B: It is completely painless compared to taking oral medications
options.C: It completely cures chronic arthritis after just one single dose
options.D: It delivers high drug concentrations directly to the target area with fewer systemic side effects

explanation: Targeting the joint directly keeps the medicine where it is needed most without flooding the entire body. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h1)

question: What is the primary function of synovial fluid inside a joint capsule?

options.B: Producing red blood cells for the limb
options.C: Anchoring muscles firmly to the bone
options.D: Lubricating the joint and nourishing cartilage

explanation: Synovial fluid acts as a natural shock absorber and lubricant while feeding the joint cartilage. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h2)

question: What happens to a joint capsule when severe inflammation occurs?

options.A: It completely dries up and fuses the bones together
options.B: It stops producing all blood supply to the limb
options.C: It produces excess fluid, creating a joint effusion
options.D: It turns into hard bone tissue overnight

explanation: Inflammation inside the joint lining triggers swelling and fluid buildup, which is called an effusion. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h2)

question: What is a common indication for an intraarticular injection?
explanation: Osteoarthritis pain that does not get better with pills is a very common reason for joint injections. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h3)

question: A patient with severe knee osteoarthritis gets no relief from oral pain relievers and physical therapy. What intervention is a nurse most likely to prepare the patient for next?
explanation: When conservative oral treatments fail for localized joint wear, doctors often step up to direct joint injections. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h3)

question: Which medication class is most commonly used to reduce severe inflammation inside an arthritic joint?
explanation: Corticosteroids are powerful anti-inflammatory drugs frequently injected into joints to calm swelling and pain. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h4)

question: What is the purpose of adding hyaluronic acid to an arthritic joint?

options.A: To permanently numb the nerves of the entire leg
options.B: To kill bacterial infections inside the joint capsule
options.C: To permanently fuse the joint bones together
options.D: To act as a viscosupplement and improve joint lubrication

explanation: Hyaluronic acid mimics natural joint fluid to provide cushioning and smooth movement. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h4)

question: Why must a nurse carefully inspect the skin over a joint before an intraarticular injection?

options.A: To determine the best clothing size for the patient
options.B: To measure the exact temperature of the surrounding muscle
options.C: To check if the patient has any permanent tattoos on the limb
options.D: To make sure there is no active skin infection that could spread into the joint

explanation: Injecting through broken or infected skin carries bacteria straight into the sterile joint space, causing severe infection. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h5)

question: A patient scheduled for an intraarticular knee injection mentions taking warfarin daily for a heart condition. What is the nurse's best initial action?

options.A: Notify the healthcare provider about the anticoagulant medication
options.B: Tell the patient to stop taking all heart pills forever
options.C: Administer an extra dose of pain medication immediately
options.D: Scrub the knee with regular soap and water

explanation: Blood thinners increase bleeding risks inside the joint, so the provider must evaluate this before proceeding. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h5)

question: What is the main reason for using strict aseptic technique during an intraarticular injection?

options.A: To keep the doctor's hands clean during the procedure
options.B: To make the injection completely painless for the patient
options.C: To prevent introducing bacteria that cause septic arthritis
options.D: To ensure the medication absorbs faster into the bloodstream

explanation: Strict sterility protects the joint capsule from dangerous bacterial infections. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which skin preparation practice is essential before performing an intraarticular puncture?

options.A: Applying warm lotion to soften the skin surface
options.B: Shaving the entire limb hair without any cleanser
options.C: Wiping the skin clean with a dry cotton ball only
options.D: Allowing the antiseptic solution to dry completely on the skin

explanation: Antiseptic agents need time to dry so they can fully kill microbes on the skin surface before the needle enters. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h6)

question: What is a 'steroid flare' that some patients experience after a joint injection?

options.A: An immediate permanent cure of all joint stiffness
options.B: A sudden rash spread all over the patient's face
options.C: A temporary increase in joint pain before the medication starts working
options.D: A permanent allergic reaction requiring emergency surgery

explanation: Some patients feel extra soreness for a day or two when steroid crystals irritate the joint before calming down. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h7)

question: What post-procedure instruction should a nurse give to a patient who just received a knee injection?

options.A: Remove the sterile bandage right away and soak in mud
options.B: Run a long distance immediately to spread the medicine
options.C: Take off all clothes and stay in a hot sauna for hours
options.D: Rest the joint and apply ice packs to reduce swelling

explanation: Resting the joint and icing it helps prevent excess irritation and controls post-injection discomfort. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h7)

question: What is the most serious potential complication of an intraarticular injection?
explanation: Infection inside the joint space is a severe and dangerous complication requiring urgent medical treatment. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h8)

question: A patient calls the clinic three days after a shoulder injection reporting a high fever, severe throbbing pain, and a hot, swollen joint. What is the nurse's best response?

options.A: Tell the patient this is a normal steroid flare and to take a warm bath
options.B: Advise the patient to exercise the shoulder vigorously to work it out
options.C: Reassure the patient that fevers always happen after joint injections
options.D: Instruct the patient to come in immediately for evaluation of potential infection

explanation: Fever, severe pain, and a hot joint are classic warning signs of a joint infection that need urgent medical review. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h8)
